title: Traffic Hemisphere Activation Matrix - Lab Notes (WIP)
content:
Purpose:

This is a working lab note that experiments with a slightly different framing for cross-functional rollouts: think of traffic partitions as "hemispheres" rather than linear percentages. The goal is to create a small, repeatable choreography for shipping interdependent LLM features that reduces blast radius while preserving signal quality for A/B analysis.

Why a hemisphere mental model?
- Encourages orthogonal slicing: split users by independent attributes (region, customer tier, client SDK version) rather than strictly by percent.
- Helps define non-overlapping guardrails for cascaded features (e.g., rerank + hallucination-filter).
- Eases rapid fallback: each hemisphere can be isolated and remapped to a fallback path without touching other slices.

Quick glossary used in this doc:
- Hemisphere: an orthogonal traffic partition; can be geographic, product-surface, or behavioral.
- Anchor cohort: a stable, high-fidelity subset used for calibration and drift checks.
- Probe traffic: synthetic or low-volume live traffic sent to exercise the entire stack (latency + correctness).
- Adaptive fence: a configurable gate that tightens or relaxes exposure based on EWMA of signals.

Activation matrix (sketch)
Columns = Hemispheres (EAP, NA-web, NA-mobile, EU, Enterprise).
Rows = Feature dimensions (model variant, rerank on/off, safety filter version, cache policy).
Cell = rollout state (off | shadow | soft-expose | full).

Example cell state progression: off -> shadow (no user-facing changes) -> soft-expose (5% within hemisphere) -> progressive (step 5%->20%->50%) -> full.

Safety guardrails (practical checklist)
- Preflight:
  - Run unit and integration smoke on staging with longest sequence tokens observed in prod (test PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-sim/pull/57).
  - Define anchor cohort (min 10k monthly active in hemisphere or synthetic equivalent).
  - Spike probe: schedule 200 synthetic queries/hour for 24h across model variants.

- Observability requirements (must be live before soft-expose):
  - Latency: P50/P95/P99, bucketed by hemisphere and route.
  - Cost: tokens per session, cost per 1k tokens, quantized by model variant.
  - Correctness: aggregate eval score on probe prompts + fuzzy-match rate for response templates.
  - Safety signals: hallucination proxy (external API mismatch), abusive content detection rate, false-positive safety-filter hits.
  - Usage-pattern regressors: session length, repeat-query rate (may indicate bad UX).

- Automation triggers (ops rules we experimented with):
  - Immediate rollback: sustained P99 > baseline by 300ms for 10m AND error rate increase > 0.5% absolute.
  - Soft-fence tighten: EWMA(1h) hallucination proxy up by 20% vs anchor cohort -> reduce hemisphere exposure by 50%.
  - Escalation -> human: any safety filter regression above threshold OR statistically significant negative business metric (CTR / conversions) vs control (p<0.01).

A/B and nested experiments pattern
- We allow nested A/B inside a hemisphere. For example NA-mobile hemisphere can test rerank A vs B with 40/40/20 split (A,B,control).
- To keep treatment independence, we bind randomization seeds to user-id + hemisphere-id so cross-hemisphere leakage is minimized.
- Metric hierarchy: primary (business outcome), secondary (quality evals), guardrail (safety proxies, latency).

Drift detection & metric sanity
- Notable experimentation: we should prefer SPC (statistical process control) using EWMA/CUSUM to spot slow drift vs classical short-window t-tests which can be noisy on large volumes.
- Use anchor cohort as baseline for signal normalization; anchor must be stable and unchanged for at least 30d before use.
- Example rule: if EWMA of normalized hallucination score crosses 3 sigma band for 2 consecutive windows (1h), flag for immediate review.

Fallback topology
- Fallbacks are layered: 
  - Local route fallback: within hemisphere, map traffic to previous model variant or disabled feature flag.
  - Cross-hemisphere degrade: if multiple hemispheres show correlated regressions, shift traffic to a fallback global path (e.g., conservative model family).
  - Kill-switch: global emergency route that serves a strict safe-only model (audited) while SRE/Prod triages.

Operational roles + communication
- Primary steward (product): owns experiment hypothesis, communication cadence.
- Serving owner (eng): readiness + rollout toggles.
- SRE: monitors alarms and triggers automated runbooks.
- Safety SME: signals on content regressions and coordinates mitigations.
- On-call rotation: 24/7 paging for immediate rollback triggers.

Suggested rollout ceremony (lean)
1) Preflight sync (15m): product, eng, SRE, safety SME — review anchor cohort, probes, and KPIs.
2) Launch soft-expose (10m): enable shadow -> probe active -> monitoring baseline.
3) First observation window (4h): daily check-ins every 30m for first 2h, then hourly.
4) Progressive expansion (if green): 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 24–72h with automated EWMA gates.
5) Hand-off to steady-state: once metrics stable for 7d, move stewardship to feature owner for long-term measurement.

Lab experiments we've run (notes)
- Experiment: hemisphere = NA-mobile; rerank A/B + default control. Observation: initial P95 up by 80ms in soft-expose but anchor-correctness improved by +3.2% on probe prompts. Decision: tightened adaptive fence for NA-mobile until model kernel patch reduces P95. (See PROJ-8421)
- Experiment: enterprise hemisphere with aggressive caching disabled to test freshness. Result: reduced hallucination proxy by 12% but increased token cost by 0.9%. Tradeoff decision deferred to commercial.

Open questions / things to try next
- Can we automate hemisphere selection via clustering of behavioral features? (e.g., use short-time embeddings of session traces to find orthogonal partitions)
- Is EWMA the right window size for low-volume hemispheres? Should we hybridize with Bayesian online change detection?
- How to surface per-hemisphere shadow results in Redwood Console without creating alert fatigue? (UX question)

To-do (short list)
- [ ] Wire probe traffic generator into rollout-sim repo and add config per hemisphere. (owner: Jon)
- [ ] Add EWMA-based alarm templates to observability dashboards (owner: Ravi)
- [ ] Document anchor cohort creation checklist as a Confluence form (owner: Maya)

References and quick links

- Github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-sim/pull/57
- Jira: PROJ-8421, PROJ-8476

Notes-to-self
- Keep language light when sharing with GTM; emphasize predictable cost/latency controls and safety fences.
- This hemisphere framing is intentionally metaphoric — needs a short explainer slide for stakeholders.

Last edit summary:
- Added adaptive fence automation rules and EWMA thresholds (2024-12-02).
- Recorded NA-mobile experiment outcome and action items.

End of lab note.
